blocks.why: Full night in your own bed before the roster starts — no alarm, you'll be awake very late tomorrow.
Siesta in the afternoon dip so you're not 16 hours awake when you cross the Atlantic tonight.
Straight to bed on arrival at the JFK hotel — 01:00 local is 07:00 body time, so keep it dark and take what comes.
Late-afternoon lie-down before the overnight home; report is 20:20 local and you'll fly straight through your body's night.
Short nap when you get home off the redeye — keep it under two and a half hours or you'll never sleep tonight.
Early to bed for a 05:40 report; alarm at 02:45Z gives you the 85-minute drive with a little slack.
Nine hours after the four-sector day — you need to bank it before a 13h30 duty to Singapore.
Land 08:10 in Singapore and go straight down — that window is still your body's small hours.
Second sleep on the Singapore night so you're properly loaded for the long haul home; up at 08:30 local with time for breakfast.
Home just after 22:00 local — into bed and let the four days off do the resetting.
Normal home night; anchor the body clock back on Madrid time.
Normal home night.
Normal home night.
Shift an hour later and sleep in — tomorrow is a 20:20 report and an all-night sector to Dubai.
Afternoon nap before the night flight; you're off home at 16:55Z so this is the last chance.
Into the Dubai hotel at 07:45 local and sleep through the morning — it's still overnight to your body.
Second, proper night in Dubai — two nights on the ground is the one chance this month to catch up.
Long afternoon nap before a 21:40 report — this flight sits right across 02:00–06:00 body time.
Home about 05:00 after the redeye — sleep the morning out; the clocks went back overnight so you gain an hour.
Get one clean Madrid night in before the Brazil pairing.
Take whatever comes late morning — you land in São Paulo at 22:25 local, which is nearly 03:00 to you.
Bed by 23:30 São Paulo time; it's the only real sleep on this short layover.
Late-morning nap in GRU before the all-night eastbound — you land 06:25 Madrid having flown the whole WOCL.
Sleep on arrival home but set an alarm for early afternoon so tonight is still sleepable.
First recovery night after Brazil — back onto Madrid nights.
Full night before standby; you cannot control what standby throws at you, so arrive rested.
Top-up before a standby window that runs to 22:00 local — banked sleep in case they call you late.
Straight to bed as the standby window closes.
Bank an afternoon nap — tomorrow's standby starts at 05:00 local and you'll not get a full night.
Unnaturally early night for a 05:00 standby start; sleep before an early never comes easy, so the nap above is your insurance.
Nap when standby releases at 14:00 local to pay back this morning's short night.
Full night before the daylight run to Dubai.
Land 22:40 local and go to bed — Dubai's night and yours line up close enough tonight.
Second Dubai night; keep the same hours so you're not chasing your clock.
Long afternoon nap before the 23:10 departure — same trick as the last DXB night flight and it worked.
Home about 05:00 off the redeye; sleep the morning, then keep the day quiet.
One night only before Boston — make it a full one, you'll be up past 24:00 body time tomorrow.
Odd-looking 15:30–23:00 Boston sleep, but it's 21:30–05:00 to your body and it's a one-night layover — don't fight the clock for 24 hours.
Big pre-duty nap before a 14:35 report and an all-night crossing landing at 05:35 Madrid.
Home by 07:30 local after the last redeye — sleep, but wake by early afternoon to salvage tonight.
First proper recovery night of the two days off.
Close the roster period on a normal Madrid night.

conflicts.statement: Every long-haul duty reports 90 minutes before off-blocks, but the 14 Oct European day reports only 60 minutes before (05:40 for a 06:40 departure). I have used the printed times as-is.
options: Confirm with crewing whether short-haul report is genuinely 60 minutes
If it is actually 90 minutes, your report is 05:10 local and you must leave home at 03:45 local — pull the whole preceding sleep forward by 30 minutes

conflicts.statement: You land back at MAD at 12:20 local on 13 Oct off an overnight from JFK, and report again at 05:40 local on 14 Oct — leaving home about 04:15 local. The sleep before an early start like that is short and low quality by definition.
options: Protect the 13 Oct afternoon nap as non-negotiable and keep it under 2h30
Ask crewing to swap the 14 Oct earliest for a later report
Consider a hotel near MAD on the night of 13 Oct to buy back the 85-minute commute

conflicts.statement: The 14 Oct duty runs 05:40 to 19:59 local — about 14h20 across four sectors, starting in the window where your body is least alert. Length and legality are the operator's call, not mine.
options: Ask the operator to confirm the FDP calculation and any extension used
Plan controlled rest in the cruise on the FRA sectors
Raise a fatigue report if you arrive at the last sector feeling degraded

conflicts.statement: 13 Oct is printed LIB, but the JFK–MAD duty does not end until 12:20 local that day. It is not a free day.
options: Query with crewing whether 13 Oct is counted toward your 15 days off
Treat it as a recovery day, not a usable day off

conflicts.statement: 16 Oct (SIN), 23 Oct (DXB) and 3 Nov (DXB) are printed LIB but you are down-route on a layover, not at home.
options: Confirm the operator counts these as layover rest days rather than days off
Do not plan anything at home around these dates

conflicts.statement: GRU gives you only about 15h40 from end of duty to next report, with your body clock still on Madrid time, ahead of a 10h20 all-night sector home landing at 06:25.
options: Take both the arrival sleep and the pre-duty nap; do not go into São Paulo
Ask for an extra night at GRU if the pattern repeats
Plan in-flight rest early in the cruise, not late

conflicts.statement: Four duties fly straight through 02:00–06:00 body time: JFK–MAD (12 Oct), DXB–MAD (24 Oct and 4 Nov), GRU–MAD (27 Oct) and BOS–MAD (7 Nov). All land at MAD between 03:10 and 06:25 local.
options: Treat the pre-duty nap before each of these as part of the duty, not optional
Split in-flight rest so you get the second half of the bunk period before descent
Do not drive home yourself after the 03:10 arrivals if you feel degraded — 85 minutes at that hour is the riskiest part of the day

conflicts.statement: European clocks go back on 25 Oct while you are airborne DXB–MAD. The roster's printed 03:10+1 arrival is already in CET, and I have converted on that basis; everything from 25 Oct onwards at MAD/FCO/FRA is UTC+1.
options: Double-check the 26 Oct GRU report of 14:35 is CET, not a stale CEST print
Reset your watch and phone before departing DXB, not after landing

conflicts.statement: Both RSV lines show MAD-MAD with no indication of airport or home standby. That changes when you must be out of bed by 85 minutes.
options: Confirm the standby type with crewing
I have planned for airport standby (leaving home 85 minutes before the window opens) as the conservative case
If it is home standby, you can hold the 1 Nov bedtime back to about 20:30 local

conflicts.statement: The 1 Nov standby opens at 05:00 local. As airport standby that means leaving home at 03:35 local, so the preceding sleep has to start around 19:45 local — a time your body will resist.
options: Take the 31 Oct afternoon nap to bank sleep
Accept a short night and plan a recovery nap when standby releases at 14:00 local
Ask whether the 30 Oct late standby and 1 Nov early standby can be swapped so they run in the same direction

conflicts.statement: Any callout on either standby day invalidates the sleep plan from that point on, and a late 30 Oct callout could run into the small hours.
options: Re-plan from the callout time using the same rule: protect the block before duty, nap in the afternoon dip
If called out late on 30 Oct, flag the 1 Nov 05:00 standby to crewing immediately

conflicts.statement: You land at 03:40 local on 5 Nov and report again at 11:10 local on 6 Nov for Boston — one civil night between two body-clock-hostile duties.
options: Keep 5 Nov completely clear of commitments
Split sleep: morning block on arrival plus a full night before Boston, as planned
Raise it with crewing if you arrive at 6 Nov already short
